articles.title: Rupee appreciates for third consecutive day as oil dips
articles.excerpt:
The rupee appreciated for the third consecutive day, opening at ₹93.30 per US dollar as crude oil prices continued to fall and market sentiment improved.

The local currency rose 18 paise at open on November 18, marking its third consecutive session of gains. It was trading at around ₹93.40 a dollar during the first few hours of the session. Rupee has appreciated by over 90 paise in the last three sessions. It last saw these levels on April 17, 2026, when it was at ₹92.60.

The increase is attributed to lower crude prices and renewed FPI interest in Indian stocks.

articles.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang $10.7 bn share transfer: CEO, wife Lory transfers 59 mn stocks to Trust - What SEC filing reveals?
articles.excerpt:
A massive transfer of Nvidia shares worth nearly $10.7 billion has brought the wealth structure of co-founder Jensen Huang and his family into focus. Months before his reported exit as the chipmaker's CEO, Huang and his wife, Lori, moved almost 59 million shares into an irrevocable family trust, according to SEC disclosures.

The transaction was part of a decade-long estate-planning arrangement involving two trusts set up in 2016. It follows the termination of two trusts established by the couple a decade earlier.

articles.title: Rupee ends flat after hitting seven-month high as firmer dollar offsets inflows
articles.excerpt:
The Indian rupee closed almost flat after peaking at a seven-month high during early trading on Wednesday. Robust foreign investments in local stocks provided a boost, but a stronger dollar capped further gains. The dollar index rose by 0.2%, reaching its highest since April 2025 due to anticipations of accelerated rate hikes.
